study.question: Does preserving chronological adjacency of complete category-brand bucket pairs retain useful information beyond unordered target-match, action-age, identity and context-overlap summaries on the same supplied causal history?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: parent source uses bags of events and log2/coarse age bins, and its receipt reports zero overlap-feature change under input reversal. Histories differing only in identity assignment to ages inside one log2 age bin can collide in every parent representation while differing in chronological recurrence. A compact directed adjacent-event contingency may recover predictive information. This is an information-retention hypothesis, not an established behavioral mechanism or novelty claim.

nearest_work.difference: Exact local parent retained, including all embedding, pooling, moment, identity, context, repeat and Gram heads. New branch uses directed consecutive singleton-time events; parent Gram considers unordered pairs of action-age contexts.

Archived arxiv v4 content SHA256 5fee25f33f375e51b3ee9417d376ff9dbe2ea3628c932a7679ddfeb0feaaade2, lines80-144 inspected. Inherits the broad concern about information loss under pooling, but new deterministic adjacency statistics are neither its local activation unit nor a DIN reproduction.

inherited_components: Frozen causal features, labels, train/validation identity, supplied128-event histories and sample coverage
All observed_overlap parent modules, modes, parameter allocation order, forward operations and initialization
Embedding dim16, hidden128/64, scratch training, host Adam/lr0.001, three epochs, seed42
Zero-initialized final residual weight and bias-free head pattern inherited from earlier local branches
study.proposed_difference: Append a parameter-matched residual to the entire parent. New support: masked complete positive category/brand pairs whose age occurs exactly once among complete valid events; remove every member of a tied timestamp, report retained support. Sort by decreasing age (oldest to newest), never infer chronology from input positions or category IDs. Source/destination cell u=4*target-match-group+action-1 has16 values. Four256-coordinate tables count adjacent edges T, category-equal edges C, brand-equal edges B, pair-equal edges J. Chronological mode uses the actual n-1 edges. Exchangeable mode uses exact expected adjacent counts under uniform permutations of the SAME n distinguishable supported events: (m_u*m_v-1[u=v]*m_u)/n, with equality-constrained analogues from identity-cell histograms. Product pairing replaces ONLY J with C*B/T (zero when T=0), retaining common T,C,B tables. All counts get log1p/log129, yielding1024 coordinates. Compute all modes before selection, no quadratic training tensor. Append1024->16->1 ReLU head, no bias, zero final weight. Four cells form a2x2 order-by-pairing factorial.
predictions: At seed42 chronological_joint will exceed exchangeable_joint on full-validation AUC if temporal adjacency adds utility conditional on the same exact unordered marginals; report Logloss and measured cost even if discordant.

Chronological_joint versus chronological_product measures incremental joint pair recurrence beyond the same chronological total/category/brand edge counts. Exchangeable_joint versus exchangeable_product provides the parallel unordered contrast; report interaction (AUC_CJ-AUC_CP)-(AUC_EJ-AUC_EP), without interpreting AUC as an additive causal scale.

Implementation invariants: both orders sum T to max(n-1,0), 0<=J<=min(C,B)<=T, identical total supported category/brand/cell masses, all modes allocate16400 new parameters and begin with exactly the parent function. Empty, missing-only and fully tied histories add zero residual.

Controlled constructed histories with the same identity multiset, target group, action and log2/coarse age bins should have equal parent representations and exchangeable features but different chronological pair recurrence. A second pairing witness should hold chronological T,C,B fixed while changing J.

Prospective constructed pairing witness confirmed in scalar implementation checks, not host data: sequences00112233 and00113223 over pairs(1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2), all action1, descending ages23..16 and target(3,3). All parent multisets and bins agree; T/C/B=7/6/4, J=4 versus3. Expected chronological-joint normalized feature gap0.0459160833; other three new readouts must agree. Host floating point parent errors require tolerance.
falsifiers: A nonzero dense-oracle/support/conservation/padding/reordering diagnostic error above float tolerance invalidates the implementation claim and blocks scientific interpretation.

If chronological_joint does not improve over exchangeable_joint at comparable measured cost, this implementation provides no support for incremental chronological utility. If it also fails versus the incumbent, retain the incumbent; failure does not refute all sequential models.

If chronological_joint fails to exceed chronological_product, reject joint-pair recurrence attribution even if chronological common edge counts improve AUC. If both pairing contrasts improve equally, evidence concerns pairing broadly, not a special chronology interaction.

If supported chronology is rare after timestamp ties are removed, or increases cost beyond the declared per-call cap, the branch is impractical under this protocol. Diagnostics are first512-impression measurements, not population estimates or independent confirmation.
alternative_explanations: Single-seed optimization noise, checkpoint selection and adaptive validation reuse across16 rounds can explain small gains; no uncertainty or significance claim without paired repetitions.
A gain may be driven by the directed action/target-match transitions in T,C,B rather than joint identity recurrence; the factorial distinguishes these readouts.
Chronological versus exchangeable contrasts change exact recency association and locality together; they do not identify causality, transition intent, direction alone, or gap-duration effects.
Removing tied timestamps and missing pairs changes only the NEW branch support and may underrepresent high-activity histories. Parent uses all original supplied events in every variant.

Product J is an empirical edge-conditional category/brand-independence replacement and need not be realizable together with all inherited observed parent statistics; it is not a randomized sequence intervention.

More readout capacity or scratch optimization can explain differences versus the historical incumbent. Within-suite comparisons are matched; an appended-zero parent confirmation is reserved if a branch is promising.

Prior within-behavior pooling was worse than DIN (0.611913 versus0.613362); event-energy branch0.619705 was worse than pooled_parent0.620094. These negative trajectories argue against assuming finer granularity always helps. Recent overlap gain over zero is only0.000135, not broad repeated support.

Exchangeable expected edge endpoints are averaged over all event permutations, while chronological endpoints are the oldest/newest retained events. Thus endpoint composition, fine-age association and adjacency are jointly changed; a favorable contrast cannot identify one of them alone.
